1754. An explicit native boundary datum for the axial-to-Landau source map; test of the identity B=log(V') bridge.

Keep all physical-law questions open. Work first in the ACTUAL native predecessor setting of CMP99 Spaces75-102 and CMP98 Averaging. This is an exact constraint-datum calculation on the original source's admitted charts, not a full change-of-measure formula, new physical family or replacement of the chosen physical M^1. CMP99Spaces81 explicitly says its Landau-image Sigma_k is not contained in the original fixed-average space. It then derives the replacement boundary datum in1.30-1.31 and uses Q_j(U0,eta A)=B in1.37. The following calculation determines that actual B for a concrete original source datum instead of assuming B is the unmodified relative coarse V'.

Source equation1.31: if a coarse bond b is oriented from b_minus in the finer site stratum Lambda_{j-1} to b_plus in Lambda_j, the GROUP target of the relative average is

 W_b = exp[-i sum_{z in B(b_minus)} L^(-d) (1/i)log((R0^(j-1) V')(Gamma_{b_minus,z}))] V'_b,
 B_b=(1/i)log W_b.

The CONTEXT and order matter. V'=V*(U0bar^j)^(-1) on the graded data, native background-relative operations R0 are exactly those of the source, Gamma lies wholly in the finer stratum, and the exponential multiplies V'_b on the LEFT for this orientation. Interior bonds whose endpoints both lie in Lambda_j have W_b=V'_b instead. No commuting of matrices, interchange of old and new means or orientation reversal is assumed. At j=1, U0=I, R0^0 is the zero-step identity on fine data.

Choose a compatible anchored OLD block B(y) with y=b_minus outside X, and its positive-first-direction neighboring coarse anchor b_plus=y+L e1 inside X. Every fine point of B(y) is in the old finer stratum, so every Gamma_{y,z} used below is allowed old data. In local coordinates y=0, B(y)={0,...,12}^4, b_plus=(13,0,0,0), and choose z_star=(1,1,0,0). This is only a translated boundary patch: embed it at a flat face of source-admissible large-block X; do not assert a loneL block satisfies M1/R. One may take the native sequence with Omega0 the entire sufficiently large torus, Omega1=X a properly aligned large box, and a coarse boundary block immediately outside it. The Omega0 separation condition is then automatic and all domain boundaries can be kept away from this patch. In the local picture X starts at first coordinate13; z_star has positive distance from X. An arbitrary fixed actual torus is not replaced in a physical theorem by this source-instance construction.

In the fixed source compact group choose a nonzero Hermitian Lie-algebra element T and a sufficiently small a>0 in its one-parameter subgroup. No G, beta_ref, g1_ref or cutoff change is made by this algebraic choice. For a concrete familiar realization one can use SU2 and T=diag(1,-1), but the argument uses only the commuting one-parameter subgroup in the fixed G. Define h(z_star)=exp(i a T), h(z)=I elsewhere, and the global flat field U'(v,w)=h(v)h(w)^(-1). Take U0=I. Let V be the ACTUAL graded source averages of U', so its old fine part is U' and every original coarse mean is I: h is I at every coarse anchor and actual old mean equivariance applies. Thus V'=V. All original plaquette holonomies and their covariant derivatives are exactly flat, and U' satisfies the source curvature regularity for every positive amplitude. It is axial in every active block of X relative to I, because h is supported strictly in an old block. The actual old fine data differ from I by O(a); choose a sufficiently small for source1.35, the relative-mean charts and Theorem2 hypotheses. This does not claim to have audited Theorem2 or proved a uniform quantitative chart threshold.

The old data on each Gamma_{y,z} telescope exactly to h(y)h(z)^(-1). They are exp(-i a T) at z=z_star and I for every other z in B(y). The principal source log on this small subgroup is therefore -aT at the exceptional point and0 elsewhere. The old-path average in1.31 is -aT/L^d. Since V'_b=I, the ACTUAL replacement target is

        W_b=exp(i a T/L^d),     B_b=a T/L^d !=0.

The naive substitution W_b=V'_b=I or B_b=log(V'_b)/i=0 is false for every sufficiently small nonzero a. For L=13,d=4 the coefficient is exactly1/28561. This is not a numerical small-factor estimate. The special fine site is not a coarse anchor. The first/last links of every old path, all old fixed exterior coordinates and all actual source relative factors are retained; the result comes from their deterministic effect, not from deleting the exterior.

This is a SOURCE datum/constraint countertest to a universal identity bridge. It does not provide an actual numerical Landau field A or gauge u, a determinant, an inverse, or a positive first-RG sector. If the native source Theorem2 is used with its admitted assumptions, its resulting A must obey the nonzero B_b above; the calculation does not assert that u=I, or that U' itself is already in Landau gauge. A proper X with this flat field has NOT been shown to arise with nonzero original P0/P1/Q1 weight; no assertion of impossibility is made either. Held P1 source issues are not repaired by this example.

The native constraint map must therefore carry the boundary functional V' -> B(V',U0), not merely rename raw V' as B. An actual normalized marked fiber map would additionally need its inverse/gauge reconstruction, the source block/root dictionary to the chosen physical M^1, the constrained Jacobian, Haar/FP factors, source action, external marks, normalizers, collars, sector labels and history. None is declared closed here. The exact boundary formula is a concrete input to that map and refutes its naive identity specialization, not a new paper or physical theorem. Falsifiers: a wrong orientation/order in1.31, an old path leaving its finer stratum, a failure of the actual original mean to give coarseI on this flat anchor-fixed field, or source axial/regularity conditions excluding the proposed sufficiently small native data. Preserve any adverse result instead of silently changing the field, domain or law.
